messages:
maria: Quick update — I rolled the split-stage scheduling branch to canary for a 30m soak. Wanted to share what I saw and get opinions on the next steps.

aj: Nice — numbers?

maria: Baseline -> canary (same hardware, same model): throughput +8% overall, average latency +5ms, p99 interactive stayed ~115ms. But we observed sporadic decode-side spikes up to ~800ms in mixed small+long workload.

devon: 800ms sounds like a handshake/kv stall rather than kernel latency. Any stack traces?

maria: Attaching a small log excerpt: 
```
[2026-02-18T18:12:21Z] decode-queue: pop req id=4352 token_budget=16 stage=decode -> selected kernel=quant-8x4
[2026-02-18T18:12:21Z] kv-cache: miss for req id=4352, warming -> fallback to full-attn on GPU0
[2026-02-18T18:12:21Z] handshake: waiting for prefill drain (prefill_queue_len=7, decode_queue_len=18)
```

maria: Looks like when prefill backlog > ~6 it delays the decode handshake and kv warmup, which forces a kernel fallback path.

aj: Interesting. Did you change the token_budget targets for decode buckets in this run?

maria: Yes — we lowered decode token_budget from 32->16 to prioritize smaller decodes and reduce tail latency for tiny prompts. That reduced avg cost but seems to trigger more kv misses because prefill is being drained more eagerly and we get more fragmented cache warmups.

samir: Could be thrash: prefill creates many small kv entries, decode hits see cold segments. Maybe increase kv prefetch window or delay decode handshake until kv ready threshold met.

devon: I think we should try two parallel experiments: (A) raise decode token_budget back to 24 and add a 50ms handshake delay when kv miss rate > 10%; (B) keep token_budget=16 but enable aggressive kv-prefetch for the next N tokens on prefill where prefix_len>32.

aj: Sounds reasonable. Also check kernel selection telemetry — the fallback path there is much heavier. We should prefer small-kernel path when seq_len<64 even if kv isn't fully warm.

maria: FYI the kernel-selection logic currently checks (kv_ready && seq_len<=64) -> use fused-kernel; else fallback. I'm proposing we make it probabilistic: if seq_len<=32 prefer fused-kernel even if kv_ready=false with a soft limit to avoid KS stalls.

samir: Probabilistic will give us signal without full rollback. Maybe ramp with sticky sampling per-worker: sample 5% -> 20% -> 100%.

ci-bot: Deploy event: canary/phase-split-v3 rolled at 2026-02-18T18:00:00Z by maria.

maria: Action items from thread: 1) devon to run two canaries (A/B) with the config diffs I noted; 2) aj to add kernel-selection telemetry counters for 'probabilistic-fused' and 'fallback-reason'; 3) samir to prototype kv-prefetch toggle (prefetch N=8) and add metric for prefetch hit-rate. I'll collect results after 2h runs.

devon: Will spin up A/B this afternoon. Will also add a small client that simulates mixed small+long workload to reproduce.

aj: I'll add the telemetry and a dashboard widget for fallback rate by worker.

maria: Thanks — if we can reduce those 800ms spikes to <200ms we're in good shape. Also note: we saw a tiny regression in throughput for long-only workloads (-1.4%), so watch tradeoffs.

samir: If we need to, we can gate probabilistic fused-kernel only on premium-tier workers to avoid impacting shared pools.

maria: Good call. I'll update the PR with config flags for tier-gating. Will post numbers in this thread when available. :thumbsup:
